feedback: When a match is correct, narrate why it works: 'The monkey's gripping tail holds on to branches as it climbs through the sunny canopy, where fruit and fresh leaves grow.'

When a mismatch is tried, show the consequence: 'On the dark floor the monkey's gripping tail has no branches to hold, and it is far from the fresh leaves and fruit growing up high — it would struggle; a tapir foraging in the litter does well here instead.'
If a child treats placement as interchangeable ('they could swap'), return to one layer's light and food and ask what that animal would eat or grip there.
activities.intendedInsight: An animal's body and its layer are a matched pair: adaptations such as a prehensile tail or hooked claws make an animal thrive in one layer and struggle in another. A rainforest packs in so much life precisely because its stacked layers create many different homes in one warm, wet place.
learnerActions: Work with a vertical cross-section from the dark forest floor up to the sunlit emergent layer, with each layer labelled by its light level and food (fruit and leaves high up; litter and decomposers on the dim, damp floor).

Place animals into the layer where their body suits them: a howler monkey or prehensile-tailed creature and a sloth with hook-like claws into the canopy; a tapir, decomposers, and a ground-hunting jaguar on the forest floor; a camouflaged ambush animal such as a snake into the dim understory; a harpy eagle or large bat in the emergent layer. (Jaguars also climb into the understory, so the sim should accept that placement too.)
For each placement, say WHY the animal fits — name the adaptation (gripping tail, hooked claws, camouflage, strong flight) and the layer demand it meets.
Try a deliberate mismatch (e.g. put the gripping-tailed monkey on the floor, or the tapir up in the canopy) and describe what would go wrong.
activities.title: Stock the rainforest: match animals to their layers

feedback: For a sorting error, revisit that layer's light and food and ask which animal body features would help there.
For the species-richness question, reinforce the combination of warmth, constant moisture, and many layered niches.
Flag the 'bright colours = hiding' choice and correct it to warning signals where relevant.
activities.intendedInsight: The child can categorise animals by layer and connect adaptations to layer demands, and can state why the habitat is so species-rich.
learnerActions: Sort a set of rainforest animals into their correct layers.
Match adaptations to the layer demand they meet (gripping tail → canopy; camouflage and ambush → dim understory; foraging/decomposing → floor; strong flight → emergent).
Answer a short question on why rainforests hold so many species (warm, wet, year-round, many niches across stacked layers).
activities.title: Sort and match check
